transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-08
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Priya Raman (Harbor AI VP Eng), Luca Bianchi (Harbor AI Head Infra), Amir Khalid (Harbor AI CPO)

Summary (auto): Customer is planning a Q1 product ramp and needs predictable capacity and EU residency for a set of use-cases. Discussed 12-month extension, dedicated capacity vs hosted, and a pilot for Private with VPC peering. Action items agreed.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey team, thanks for joining. Quick rollcall then we'll walk through the ask — Priya, Luca, Amir, you good?
[00:06] Priya Raman: Yep, all good. Thanks Maya.
[00:09] Amir Khalid: hi, sorry running a bit late, all set now.
[00:12] Ethan Park: great. So agenda: capacity bump, eu-edge, pricing options for a one year commit, and next steps on the security and pilot.
[00:20] Priya Raman: high level — by mid Q1 we expect an uptick, probably around 3x token volume vs today, some of that is latency sensitive, customer chat and 1:1 recommendations. We need euro data residency for EU users, can't route PII out of region.
[00:37] Luca Bianchi: yeah, and we need to understand peering/egress costs — we currently do VPC peering through our cloud transit, so networking differences matter. Also curious about the dedicated pool sizing and whether we can burst.
[00:52] Maya Chen: totally. Two parts — product / ops and commercial. On the ops side Redwood offers Dedicated reserved pools, you can pin models and get predictable throughput. For EU we can provision an EU-edge cluster — that keeps data in-region and you can optionally use our Private package later. Commercially, a 12-month commit gets better unit pricing and guaranteed capacity.
[01:10] Priya Raman: quick Q — if we go 12 months with a commit, do we still get fallback to hosted if capacity hits a spike?
[01:15] Ethan Park: good question. Yes, you can configure fallback policies — by model variant or region. For example, critical traffic can fail over to hosted with a rate-limit so you don't drop requests. There is a small cross-region egress charge if you route cross-region, we'll call that out in the quote.
[01:34] Amir Khalid: and SOC2, encryption — procurement will need SOC2 report and details on KMS integration. We use a customer-managed KMS for keys today.
[01:42] Maya Chen: noted — we'll attach SOC2 and our KMS/HSM integration docs. For Private we support customer KMS via KMS integrations or HSM.
[01:50] Luca Bianchi: can you speak to the latency profile — eu-edge vs hosted? Our target p95 < 200ms for chat flows.
[01:58] Ethan Park: baseline — hosted in eu-central gets you ~120–180ms p95 for 2k context when measured from eu region. EU-edge colocated with your region reduces network hops; for large context like 4k it helps KV cache locality. But depends on workload; we'll run a throughput test.
[02:22] Priya Raman: okay, good. Commercially — we need predictable unit price per 1MM tokens, what's the delta if we do 12 vs 24 months?
[02:30] Maya Chen: rough ranges today — 12-month commit gives ~18–22% discount vs on-demand hosted; 24-month can push to 25–30% depending on volume commitment. We'll put exact tiers in the quote.
[02:43] Amir Khalid: and if we want private later, is that a migration with downtime? We can't have more than 5 minutes for cutover windows on the chat platform.
[02:51] Ethan Park: migration options — cold cutover has more downtime, but we can do staged dual-write with prefix cache warmup to lower cutover to under five minutes in many cases. We'll need a tech runbook and a dry run; SE to own that.
[03:08] Luca Bianchi: good to hear. Also our infra team will want to validate KV cache behavior — is the cache single-tenant on Dedicated?
[03:16] Ethan Park: on Dedicated, KV cache is isolated per tenant and we have cache warming tools. For Private it's fully customer controlled. There may be small warmup overhead for cold starts.
[03:28] Priya Raman: procurement timeline — Amir, where are we?
[03:31] Amir Khalid: we're targeting to sign by end of December if pricing matches expectations. PO approver list is two people — me and the CFO. We need a clean SOW and a PO template.
[03:42] Maya Chen: we'll send a PO template and SOW draft. I'll include the procurement contact flow.
[03:48] Priya Raman: can we also get an estimated monthly cost curve at tiers: baseline, +2x, +3x? Helps to plan budgets.
[03:56] Maya Chen: yes — we'll include projection bands based on your current usage and the 3x projection.
[04:05] Ethan Park: on benchmarks — to be thorough, we'll run a throughput test for your 4096-context generation jobs. We'll need a sample prompt set and a target concurrency. Luca, can you share current concurrency and cluster layout?
[04:18] Luca Bianchi: currently 8 nodes behind a load balancer, we run k8s, and we target 50 concurrent sessions for chat; for some batch gen it's higher. I'll share a topo diagram and the peering contacts.
[04:30] Priya Raman: one more nuance: some EU customers require data residency plus contractual clause for data processing. Can Redwood support a DPA addendum for EU data residency?
[04:40] Maya Chen: yes — standard DPA with data residency clauses is available. We'll attach a redlined template.
[04:45] Amir Khalid: are there any hidden costs e.g., egress, model quantization surcharges?
[04:50] Maya Chen: main extras are egress and optional model conversion/quantization assistance if you want Redwood Optimize help. We'll call those out as optional professional services.
[05:02] Ethan Park: quick note on kernels — sorry for the nerd bit — some of the open models behave better with specific kernel paths; we can pick quantized variants to reduce cost with minimal quality loss for certain workloads.
[05:18] Priya Raman: thanks. Pricing sensitivity — if you give us a 12-month with a dedicated pool and EU-edge, we need commitments on latency SLOs and a credits-based SLA.
[05:28] Maya Chen: agree. We'll include SLO targets at the committed level and define SLA credits for breaches.
[05:36] Amir Khalid: timeline to provision EU-edge — how long?
[05:40] Ethan Park: typically 2–3 weeks to provision and validate clusters once the contract is signed and infra peering is set. If you want faster there's an expedited option.
[05:50] Luca Bianchi: good. Also we have a compliance gate — security questionnaire (SIG) that needs answers. Can Redwood fill that in?
[05:58] Maya Chen: yes — we'll fill out the SIG and provide SOC2, penetration test summary, and the KMS integration doc.
[06:05] Priya Raman: okay wrap up — do we have agreement in principle that a 12-month extension with a dedicated EU pool and an option for Private pilot is the path?
[06:12] Amir Khalid: yes in principle, subject to final pricing and benchmarks.
[06:16] Maya Chen: great. Next steps recap: I'll send updated quote + SOW + PO template + SOC2 + DPA by Friday (2027-12-10). Ethan will schedule the performance benchmark and SE deep dive for 2027-12-15. Luca to share infra docs by 2027-12-13. Amir to confirm procurement approver list by 2027-12-12.
[06:40] Priya Raman: thanks everyone. Anything else?
[06:44] Luca Bianchi: one small ask — can we get an example runbook for the prefix cache warmup? That'd help our SREs.
[06:50] Ethan Park: yes, we'll include a runbook and a rehearse checklist.
[06:55] Maya Chen: perfect. Thanks all. We'll follow up in email with links — pricing sheet (link), SOC2 (link), DPA template (link).
[07:04] Amir Khalid: thanks. Bye.

Meeting close.
